chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the infant, whether it is breastfed for more than two years, so he said, 'Two years.' I said, 'And if it exceeds two years, is there anything [penalty or ruling] upon its parents regarding that?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.شَيْءٌ: anything (referring to a ruling or penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a child is breastfed for more than two years according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that while two years is the normative duration for breastfeeding, exceeding this period carries no legal penalty or sin for the parents. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding child-rearing practices, distinguishing between the recommended sunnah and obligatory limits. The absence of a penalty highlights the principle of ease in familial obligations, provided the child's welfare is maintained.
